question: Should this PR continue as the vehicle for OpenClaw's default-on multi-user memory isolation contract after the bugs are repaired, or should the work move back to the canonical design tracker?
rationale: This PR defines a new privacy/security boundary plus config defaults, so automation cannot choose the permanent product contract or accept an incomplete isolation surface on maintainers' behalf.

options.title: Repair and prove this PR
options.body: Keep this PR open, require the default/config fixes, resolve conflicts, and add redacted two-user Gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Move design to the tracker
options.body: Pause this PR and use the canonical tracker to settle the memory partition model before accepting code.

options.title: Close and request a narrower replacement
options.body: Close this branch only if maintainers decide the current diff is too stale or broad to salvage safely.

recommendation.title: Repair and prove this PR
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open, require the default/config fixes, resolve conflicts, and add redacted two-user Gateway proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent memory-core boundary/refactor history among the likely owners identified here.
